case.background: A collimated alpha beam strikes a thin metal foil. A rotatable detector counts particles emerging at selected angles. Vary material, calibrated target-nucleus areal density, exposure, and angle to infer the scattering response.
initial_observations: Most incident particles are not detected at large angles.
Rare large deflections are nevertheless reproducible above background.

controls.description: Detector angle relative to the incident beam.
controls.name: scattering_angle_deg

controls.description: Atomic number of the available foil.
controls.name: foil_atomic_number

controls.description: Calibrated number of target nuclei per unit beam area relative to the reference target.
controls.name: target_areal_number_density_relative

controls.description: Incident exposure relative to the reference beam.
controls.name: exposure_relative

instruments.description: A collimated alpha source, thin foils, rotatable detector, and exposure monitor.
instruments.name: alpha_foil_scattering_scope

notes: All targets remain in the thin, single-scattering regime.
Source energy, detector solid angle, and beam geometry remain fixed.
Target areal number density is independently calibrated, so equal settings mean equal target nuclei per unit beam area across materials.
Available foil atomic numbers are 13, 29, 47, and 79.
